steps.content: [Black Screen Background, Loop Typewriter Sound Effect for 3 Seconds]
Hello there, dear stranger. Have you ever heard of detective novels?
[Then transition to Small CG: Story Being Written]
<size=42><color=#7683a2>[DISMYTH] [Chat Room]</color> [Looking for that detective novelist who's been the talk of the town lately...]</size>

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: Question, does anyone know what the author of "The Patricia Mystery" has been up to lately?

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: It's my first time reading this kind of novel. I tried guessing along as the story goes, but I never could've guessed who the culprit really was. Can't say I was all that impressed at the start, but now I'm completely hooked...

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: I'm dying to read the sequel! When's the author releasing a new book?!

<color=#ff007f>- The Rules of Detective Novels -
I. The culprit must be someone who has appeared in the story, all the while being someone beyond the reader's expectations.</color>

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: Detective novels? What's that?

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: It's a mystery crime genre where a detective solves murder cases. I think it used to be popular before Nightfall, and this author single-handedly brought it back into the spotlight recently. She's been doing tons of interviews and promotions lately. Pretty much the most celebrated bestselling author in Eastside right now.
<color=#ff007f>II. The detective must not solve the case through supernatural or bizarre methods;</color>

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: Fr, can't wait for her next work. I finished this one in a single sitting too. Never expected the culprit to be *spoiler warning*! I kept thinking about who was more suspicious, but it turns out the killer was in front of us all along.

<color=#7683a2>Not_Going_Out_Today</color>: Good news: it's very realistic. Bad news: it's TOO realistic. I'm lowkey traumatized, legit been double-checking whether I've locked my door when I get home lately...

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: Ikr! Hands down one of the best storytellers in all of Eastside 0v0

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: But... speaking of this author...

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: Have you guys heard <color=#fb9259>that rumor</color>?
<color=#ff007f>III. The crime scene must not have more than one secret room or passageway;</color>

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: She blew up out of nowhere. Literally overnight. Even her debut work swept the charts. Whenever someone asks about her inspiration, she always says she draws ideas from real life. I thought that was the case at first, but...

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: Every time one of her stories gets published, matching "coincidences" actually happen in reality.

<color=#ff007f>IV. The detective must not solve cases through coincidences or unfounded intuition,
nor through clues that were never revealed to the reader;</color>

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: In one of her books, the killer hid the murder weapon inside a piano. That same day, news broke about a pianist committing a crime of passion. Another time, her novel featured a victim who died in a family conspiracy, and right after, a fratricidal feud in a wealthy family came to light...
<color=#ff007f>V. The detective must not be the criminal.</color>

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: She's written so many stories that are way too realistic. If you also consider all these coincidences... What if...

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: What if <color=#fb9259>she was never writing fiction to begin with?</color>

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: ...

<color=#7683a2>Not_Going_Out_Today</color>: ...

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: ...

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: Lmfao no way! We live in a civilized society, she just has a really vivid imagination, that's all... Yeah, that's definitely it!

<color=#7683a2>Not_Going_Out_Today</color>: Quite the conspiracy theorist, aren't you? How bout you go hang out with that troll from the other thread.

<color=#dg1f1f>Administrator</color>: *WARNING* The internet is not a lawless zone. Do not believe or spread unverified rumors.

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: @Da3m0n, stop lurking, your fave's back.

<color=#fb9259>Da3m0n [OP]</color>: ?! You serious? Where?!

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: The publisher just posted an announcement. Her next book's coming out soon.
<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: The new book's synopsis looks pretty interesting. The title's kind of a mouthful though, real hard to pronounce. I think it was—
The clacking of the typewriter gradually fades to silence. Another page gets filled with words, and the woman finally stops.
Phew...
The typist pauses briefly, then takes out a fresh sheet and hits the keys one final time, putting down the story's title.
[Cut to Black Screen]
Murder on the Praeva Express
[Switch to a paper texture background, see if we can borrow one from the ED background images]

CHAPTER 01: The Important Passenger on the Platform A whistle blares. An old-fashioned steam train stops at the platform. It's unusually lively inside the carriages today. The attendant, who's unfortunately on duty, finally gets a chance to take a breather from her hectic work. She leans against the train car for a quick break.
But then, out of the blue, a shadow is cast over her. The attendant scrambles to straighten up and greets them. "Good day, sir. May I see your ticket?" she says.
steps.female_content: But then, out of the blue, a shadow is cast over her. The attendant scrambles to straighten up and greets them. "Good day, ma'am. May I see your ticket?" she says.

steps.content: The passenger, dressed in a trench coat and wearing a narrow-brimmed hat, looks up, then hands over the ticket and identification to the attendant.
[Scene Transition - Train Corridor]

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Let's see here... Yup, everything's in order! Please, board the train!
The young attendant glances at the name on the document.

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: Welcome aboard the Praeva Express—we wish you a pleasant journey, Mr. ${PlayerName}!
steps.female_content: Welcome aboard the Praeva Express—we wish you a pleasant journey, Ms. ${PlayerName}!
